findings.explanation: replace('.', ...) with a string pattern escapes only the first dot. For 'eu.pay.example' the regex keeps an unescaped dot, so 'https://eu.payXexample' is allowed although it is not a configured domain or subdomain.

SORT_PATTERN has the m flag, so ^ and $ match at line boundaries. A sort such as 'name\nid; DROP TABLE x' passes validation because one line matches, and the arbitrary text is then placed in the ORDER BY clause instead of throwing.

hasMore uses end < items.length - 1 instead of end < items.length. When exactly one element follows the page, hasMore is false and collectAll drops that element, for example the last item of an array whose length is one more than a multiple of pageSize.

deposit adds amount to balance with no upper bound check. Depositing into a balance at or near Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER makes balance exceed the safe-integer range, violating the post-condition that balance stays a safe integer.

When the provider supplies role as a string, includes() does substring matching on that string. hasRole({role:'owner'}, 'own') is true, and canManageBilling({role:'owner-billing'}) is true although the user's role is not exactly 'owner' or 'billing-admin'.
Math.trunc(amount * 100) truncates floating-point error. toPence(19.99) gives 1998 and toPence(0.29) gives 28 instead of 1999 and 29, and splitAmount inherits the wrong total. Math.round is needed.

The check rejects only a leading '//'. '/\\evil.example' and '/<tab>/evil.example' pass, but the WHATWG parser treats backslash as slash and strips tab, so they resolve to another origin. The trimmed candidate is returned instead of '/'.
